Recent indicators and the 25 bp cut point to a small, forecast-based easing as inflation moves toward—but remains above—2 percent. Balanced risk language, continued QT, and a hawkish dissent temper the dovishness. The September 2024 Financial Stability Report (FSR) reinforces this caution: it notes tight bank lending standards (SLOOS), ongoing monitoring of CRE and funding risks, and growth in runnable money-like liabilities, even as banks’ risk-based capital and HQLA remain solid and reliance on uninsured deposits has fallen; hedge funds also deleveraged in August. With the Fed also monitoring U.S. fiscal sustainability and geopolitical tensions, the FSR backdrop supports a restrained easing stance rather than an aggressive pivot. Net: mildly dovish, but more constrained than the statement alone implies.
